title: add jsonschema strict-mode with improved error reporting and OpenAI compatibility for response_format
author: Anika Patel
release_notes: Added strict JSON Schema validation mode for structured output (response_format). Improved error messages with OpenAI-compatible shape and clear guidance for fallbacks; default behavior unchanged. Backwards-compatible opt-in via response_format.strict
description:
Context and motivation: Users are increasingly relying on structured output (response_format) to validate LLM responses with a provided JSON Schema. We observed two recurring issues in production: 1) silent schema mismatches that get accepted downstream and cause customer regressions, and 2) error messages that are hard to map to user-facing API behavior or to OpenAI-compatible tooling. This PR introduces a strict validation mode plus an OpenAI-compatible error reporting shape and improves partial-validation fallbacks.

Summary of changes: Implement response_format.strict (boolean) that toggles "strict" validation against jsonschema. When strict=true, responses that fail schema validation are rejected at the server boundary with a deterministic error payload. When strict=false (default), we keep the existing best-effort semantics but include a new validation.delta field in the response metadata to help clients detect issues. We also add an OpenAI-compatibility layer for error objects (type/message/path/validation_details) to make integration with existing SDKs and tools simpler.

Commits (high-level): - 7c5a2e8: add response_format.strict flag and parsing on the API surface - 1b9f3c1: jsonschema validator integration and strict-mode gating - d4a7e0b: improved error object schema and OpenAI-compat mapping - 2f8c9aa: unit + integration tests for strict/non-strict flows and streaming interaction - 4e11b3f: docs, examples and SDK compatibility shim for Python/TS - 9a2b45d: fix race in streaming validation hook (hotfix after CI failure)

Files changed (high-level): - server/api/response_format.go: new parsing + validation pipeline hooks - runtime/validation/jsonschema_validator.go: validator wrapper + improved error mapping - runtime/validation/streaming_validator.go: streaming-compatible partial validation with checkpointing - sdk/python/redwood/response_format.py: compatibility shim and examples - sdk/ts/src/responseFormat.ts: types and mapping helpers - docs/api/response_format.md: doc updates and migration notes - tests/integration/test_jsonschema_strict.py: integration scenarios - ci/workflows/validate-response-format.yaml: added new matrix for schema lib versions

Behavior and compatibility notes: - Default behavior unchanged: if response_format.strict is omitted or false, we do non-blocking validation that adds metadata but does not abort generation. - Strict mode (true) will cause the request to fail fast on validation errors. The server returns a 400 with an OpenAI-compatible error object and a short example of the failing fragment to help users iterate. - Streaming: for streaming responses we buffer validation checkpoints; if a final validation fails in strict mode we terminate the stream and emit a final error frame compatible with our streaming protocol and OpenAI-compatible clients. This required a small change to the stream termination handshake (see streaming_validator.go). - SDKs: Python/TS shims expose a helper that rethrows server error into a structured ValidationError that mirrors OpenAI's shape for easier migration. - Rollouts: feature gated and dark-launched for "redwood" tenants; default off for older API clients until 2026-03-15 (migration window).

Review conversation (highlights): - Marco Ruiz (review): "Overall looks good. Two requests: please ensure the error object includes the schema pointer (JSON Pointer) and a short code we can use for metrics/auditing." - Author (Anika): "Added schema_pointer and error_code in the mapped object; updated tests." - Lina Zhang (review): "Concerned about latency for very large schemas in strict mode. Can we add a config for schema validation timeouts per-tenant?" - Author: "Added tenant-level timeout config with a 500ms default. When validation times out we return a specific error_code 'validation_timeout' and in non-strict mode we mark delta with timeout=true." - Omar Haddad (approve): "nit: add one more integration test asserting streaming termination frame shape." - Author: "Added test and fixed stream termination handshake race reported by CI."

CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (matrix): pass after rerun (one flaky test fixed in d4a7e0b) - Lint: pass - Performance: micro-benchmark added; strict mode adds ~0.8ms median validation overhead on small schemas, ~12ms on large nested schemas (within configured timeout). We added a guard to avoid tail-latency regressions for latency-sensitive routes.

Edge cases and follow-ups: - We need to track metric: response_format.validation.failures and validation.latency by tenant. ENG-7241 will add dashboards. - Follow-up: support for schemas with $ref fetching should be sandboxed; created ENG-7302 to track safe remote resolution for user-provided schemas. - Docs: migration guide, example error handling in streaming clients, and SDK docs included in this PR but will be expanded in a follow-up docs patch.

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals (Marco/Lina/Omar) and green CI.

If you want to test locally: - run `make test-integration TEST=test_jsonschema_strict.py` - use python SDK helper `redwood.response_format.validate_or_raise(schema, strict=True)` to reproduce error mapping

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps strict mode opt-in to avoid breaking behavior for existing customers. The OpenAI-compatible error shape should make it straightforward for existing OpenAI integrations to adopt strict validation with minimal client changes.
notes: dark-launch gated; default off for older clients; tenant timeout default 500ms; metrics to follow-up (ENG-7241)
